authority.tenantAuthority: A topic or channel identifier is never authority; the server derives tenant and subject ownership from trusted authentication context plus current tenant state.
authority.subjectAuthority: The authenticated subject and current membership determine who may publish or consume an event.
authority.outboxAuthority: Committed domain changes emit an outbox row in the same transaction; the outbox row is downstream durable evidence, not the business truth.
authority.deliveryAuthority: Private Realtime and NATS consumers are progressive delivery mechanisms only.

rules: eventId is a UUID; schemaVersion selects the wire contract and idempotencyKeyDigest/payloadDigest use the exact SHA-256 wire format. Neither digest is authorization proof.
organizationId, subjectId, actorId, resourceType and resourceId are server-derived from trusted context, not browser input.
topic follows scope:tenant-or-resource-id:purpose and is only a routing candidate.
safePayload contains allowlisted IDs, versions, job state and safe display metadata only.
No body, prompt, token, secret, raw provider output, unbounded PII or cross-tenant identifier may appear in the envelope or payload.
A safeDisplay value is an exact fixed catalog label, status and variant tuple only; it is never user-authored display text.
operation is derived only from the eventType routing matrix. A client may never select or override it.

payloadDigest.canonicalBytes: UTF-8 bytes of nexora:event-payload:1.1\n followed by RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON for safePayload.
payloadDigest.verification: The receiver recomputes this digest from the received safePayload and rejects a mismatch before accepting or publishing the envelope.

idempotencyKeyDigest.canonicalBytes: UTF-8 bytes of nexora:event-idempotency:1.1\n followed by RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON for {operation, organizationId, topic, eventType, resourceType, resourceId, opaqueIdempotencyKey}; no delimiter ambiguity is permitted.
idempotencyKeyDigest.verification: The producer computes it from the server-derived routing scope plus the opaque request key. The raw opaque key is never emitted; receivers validate the exact wire format, envelope immutability and scope rather than reconstructing it.

rules: Digest inputs are server-derived canonical bytes and are never a user name, email, token or arbitrary opaque string.
A producer must reject a value that fails the exact wire format before creating an outbox row or publishing.
Known-answer vectors in the M3-T01 fixture bind canonical inputs to both digest fields; a format-valid digest with a different preimage is rejected.

matrix.ownership: current ACTIVE membership for the tenant
current ACTIVE membership for the tenant
current ACTIVE membership for the resource owner
current ACTIVE membership for the tenant
current ACTIVE membership for the resource owner
current ACTIVE membership for the tenant

rules: The server chooses operation, scope, tenant/resource identifier and purpose from current ownership facts and event type.
Clients may not invent an operation, resource type, scope or purpose outside this matrix.
The identifier alone never grants access or publish rights.

topicVocabulary.ownership: The owner id encoded in the topic is derived from current server-authorized tenant or resource identity and current ACTIVE membership; guessing it never grants access.

ownership.subjectRule: Only the current ACTIVE membership for the authenticated subject may authorize publish or consume rights.
ownership.resourceRule: A guessed subjectId, membershipId, organizationId or resourceId never grants access by itself.
ownership.crossTenantRule: Cross-tenant or unowned subject guesses fail closed.

lease.claim: bounded row lease owned by one publisher at a time
lease.expiry: lease expiry makes the row reclaimable
lease.reclaim: expired or failed claims may be retried until bounded attempts are exhausted

rules: Business row and outbox row are committed in one transaction.
Claims use bounded locking or lease semantics and are idempotent.
Duplicate publish attempts never create a second logical effect.
A terminal failure is visible and never silently dropped.

idempotency.requestKey: A publish or job submission carries one opaque idempotency key digest scoped to organizationId, topic, eventType, resource identity and the operation derived from eventRouting.matrix.
idempotency.sameRequest: A retried request with the same fingerprint reuses the original terminal receipt without creating another outbox row.
idempotency.differentRequest: A reused key with a different fingerprint fails closed with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
idempotency.retention: Reuse safety after expiry is a future persistence policy; the contract does not promise it.

valueRules.resourceType: must match the eventRouting.matrix resourceTypes entry for envelope eventType
valueRules.unicode: All strings are valid I-JSON strings; lone UTF-16 surrogates are rejected before RFC 8785 canonicalization.

rules: No nested objects or arrays.
No free-form text, user identifier, content excerpt, localized copy or arbitrary status is permitted.
label, status and variant must match one exact statusVariants tuple for the envelope eventType entry in safeDisplayCatalog.
Clients map the fixed catalog keys to locally reviewed copy after durable authorization; the catalog value itself is not display copy.
jobState and progress appear together only for JOB_PROGRESS_CHANGED; both are required for that event type and forbidden for every other event type.
Every safePayload scalar must match valueRules and exactly mirror the equivalent server-derived envelope field where one exists.

compatibility.legacySchemaVersionPolicy: Ingress and consumers reject 1.0.0 envelopes fail closed because their free-form safeDisplay shape cannot establish this contract's PII boundary.
compatibility.persistenceHandoff: M3-DB01 must quarantine or dead-letter legacy rows rather than silently reserializing them as 1.1.0; M3 runtime owners must record explicit conversion evidence before accepting older inputs.
compatibility.eventVersionRule: eventVersion is business-event evolution and does not substitute for schemaVersion.

limitations: This contract defines no migration, producer implementation, worker code, browser UI, provider call or hosted behavior.
Private Realtime and NATS delivery remain downstream implementation and evidence work.
M3-DB01 owns migration/index/policy DDL; M3-T02/T03/T04/T05 own runtime consumers.
